title: Savitri and Satyavan
text:
Savitri, daughter of King Ashvapati, chose as her husband Satyavan, the son of a blind king who had lost his throne and lived in exile in the forest. The sage Narada warned her that Satyavan had every virtue but would die exactly one year from that day. Savitri refused to change her choice, and married him.

She kept the prophecy to herself. As the fatal day approached, she fasted for three days and nights, and on the morning itself she insisted on going with Satyavan into the woods to cut firewood. There he felt a sudden pain in his head and lay down with it in her lap. Yama, the lord of death, appeared and drew out his life.

When Yama set off southward, Savitri followed. He told her to turn back, but she kept walking and spoke to him so wisely about virtue and friendship that he offered her a boon, anything except her husband's life. She asked for her father-in-law's sight, then his kingdom, then sons for her own father. Each time she kept following.

Finally Yama granted her a hundred sons by Satyavan. She pointed out that this was impossible unless her husband lived. Caught by his own promise, and pleased with her, Yama released Satyavan, who woke in her lap as if from sleep.
lesson: Persistence works best when joined to clear thinking. Keep showing up for the people you love, and look for the honest argument that changes the situation.
source: Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Aranyaka Parva), Pativrata Mahatmya
